clue.text: Only a quarter are not heels!

parts.note: only, as in sole survivor, means single, one and no more
S, south, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: An exclamation that just one part in four of something is not a heel.
explanation.walkthrough: The parts of a shoe under the foot that are not the heels; 'are' makes the definition a plural verb phrase standing for a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: The underside of a shoe is divided into heel and the remaining flat part on which the foot treads.

clue.text: Caught with strong drink, beat it!

parts.note: an animal caught in a trap has been snared
rum is a strong spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: Someone nabbed with hard liquor is told to clear off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beat it!' reads as 'go away!', but it is literally an instruction to strike the thing defined.
explanation.definitionFit: This percussion instrument is played by striking it with sticks, so it is the thing you beat.

clue.text: He is defeated about sunrise

indicators.note: in a down clue a rise reads the letters upwards, so the pieces before it go backwards

parts.note: re is Latin for about, concerning
Sol is the Latin name for the sun

explanation.surface: Someone is beaten at around dawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The one word 'sunrise' does two jobs in its halves: the first half is a piece and 'rise' is the upward turn in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone beaten in a contest is the one who did not win it.

clue.text: One could well wind up eating this

definitions.text: One could well wind up eating this

parts.words: One could well wind up eating this
parts.note: winding up suggests ending up, but strands of a pasta are wound round the fork before eating

explanation.definitionFit: Long thin Italian pasta strands are twirled around a fork before being eaten.

clue.text: Military parade occurring in spring?

explanation.definitionFit: Troops filing ceremonially before a dignitary is a parade; read as a phrase it means after the third month of the year, early in spring.

clue.text: Guy's found a way to get a ridged roof

parts.note: a guy is a man, so guy's is man's
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A fellow discovers a method of building a peaked roof.
explanation.definitionFit: A roof with two slopes on each side, the lower one steeper, named after the architect Mansart.

clue.text: Savoury food — undercooked and little of it

parts.note: rare meat is lightly cooked and still red inside
a little of something is a bit

explanation.surface: A complaint about a dish that is both underdone and skimpy.
explanation.walkthrough: Welsh rarebit is cheese melted on toast, a British savoury.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheese melted on toast, also called Welsh rabbit, is a classic British savoury snack.

clue.text: Warm to the Spanish inn

parts.note: very warm means hot
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Someone takes a liking to a Spanish guesthouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are establishments offering lodging and meals to travellers.

clue.text: Entering a strange country

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the words beside it are made odd, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone arrives in an unfamiliar foreign land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strange' rearranges ENTERING plus A; 'the Argentine' is an older name for the country Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: The nation in South America was long called the Argentine, after its Spanish name Argentina.

clue.text: An article about soldiers — Kipling's perhaps

indicators.note: about means going round, so one word is placed around the other

parts.note: the is the definite article
RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army soldiers

explanation.surface: A piece of writing about troops, perhaps by Rudyard Kipling.
explanation.walkthrough: Kipling wrote the stories 'Soldiers Three'; the number is what Kipling's soldiers were.
explanation.definitionFit: Kipling's collection Soldiers Three names the number of his trio of army privates.

clue.text: Seat in bar possibly taken by non-drinker

indicators.note: possibly suggests these letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A stool in a pub is occupied by someone who does not touch alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains from alcohol is a teetotaller, refusing drink.

clue.text: Beastly assumption advocated in war by Henry V

definitions.text: Beastly assumption advocated in war by Henry V

parts.words: Beastly assumption advocated in war by Henry V
parts.note: in Shakespeare's play the king urges his troops to imitate the action of a fierce big cat

explanation.definitionFit: In Henry V the king tells soldiers to assume the manner of a striped jungle cat in battle.

clue.text: For part of the year the fox is protected here

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A remark that a fox is under protection during some months.
explanation.definitionFit: A fox's den or burrow, where it shelters underground, is its earth.

clue.text: One might get to ride in this if patient

definitions.text: One might get to ride in this if patient

parts.words: One might get to ride in this if patient
parts.note: patient reads as willing to wait, but it is the sick person carried to hospital

explanation.definitionFit: A vehicle carrying the sick or injured to hospital is ridden in by a hospital patient.

clue.text: Lay in the grass, it's alleged

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet places
to lay something down is to put it

explanation.surface: Someone is said to have lain in the grass.
explanation.definitionFit: Something said to be so, generally believed but unproven, is reputed or alleged.

clue.text: For dream furnishing

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
a vision is a dream or imagined sight

explanation.surface: A phrase about supplying a home with fittings as one imagined.
explanation.definitionFit: Supplying or equipping someone with something is providing them, a sense of furnishing.

clue.text: Ferreting out a casual shirt ' before running

parts.note: a T-shirt is a casual shirt, abbreviated to T
running in a race is racing

explanation.surface: A man in a T-shirt hunts for something before going for a run.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray ' in the clue is a print mark, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tracking down or following the trail of something is uncovering it by search.

clue.text: The glorification of contemporary speech

parts.note: AD, anno Domini, marks the present era, so it stands for contemporary
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: A remark about how modern talk praises things.
explanation.definitionFit: Worshipful praise and honour given to someone is a form of glorification.

clue.text: Most agree to organise a fuel store

indicators.note: to organise letters is to put them in a new order

explanation.surface: Most people consent to set up a fuel depot.
explanation.definitionFit: A gasholder is a large tank storing town gas, a fuel.

clue.text: Heath and his playing of Othello?

parts.note: a moor is open heathland

indicators.note: playing makes the letters of the word beside it move about

explanation.surface: An actor named Heath and his performance as Shakespeare's Othello.
explanation.walkthrough: Othello is the Moor of Venice, so anything belonging to him is of the Moor.
explanation.definitionFit: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor, so his qualities are those of the Moors.

clue.text: Capital security device for women

parts.note: capital suggests a city but means of the head, a clip securing a woman's tresses

explanation.definitionFit: A U-shaped pin holds a woman's hair in place on her head.

clue.text: Crowd round the senior officer for the course

indicators.note: round places one piece around the other

parts.note: to crowd is to press
OC is Officer Commanding, a senior officer

explanation.surface: People throng about a commanding officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A course of action or series of steps is a process.

clue.text: Stick with old city scientist

parts.note: paste sticks things together
Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia

explanation.surface: Gluing something to an ancient town, a researcher works.
explanation.definitionFit: Louis Pasteur was the French chemist behind pasteurisation and vaccines.

clue.text: Keeps mother in fashionable satin

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: fashionable is read as able to be fashioned, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Mum wears trendy satin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like it gives IN, but IN is the clue's own word and 'fashionable' rearranges SATIN into TAINS.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something in good condition is to look after it, preserve it.

clue.text: Add up to one hundred notes

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to add is to sum
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: Instructions to total a hundred banknotes.
explanation.definitionFit: Notes played in sequence form a melody, the stuff of a tune.

clue.text: The gratitude of a Greek character

parts.note: ta is British slang for thank you

explanation.surface: The thanks of someone from Greece.
explanation.definitionFit: The eighth letter of the Greek alphabet is one of its characters.

clue.text: Warning nearly everybody to acquire a weapon

indicators.note: nearly means a word short of its final letter

parts.note: everybody means all
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: A caution that almost everyone is getting armed.
explanation.definitionFit: A signal warning of danger is an alarm.

clue.text: Notice people inside get better

indicators.note: inside places one piece within another

parts.note: an ad, advertisement, is a public notice
men are people

explanation.surface: Seeing people indoors improve.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve something by correcting it is to amend it.

clue.text: A high point for church-goers

parts.note: a high point sounds like a highlight, but it is a church's tall pointed tower

explanation.definitionFit: The tall tapering top of a church tower is literally its highest point.

clue.text: Leader giving small coin to players in regular payment

parts.note: P stands for a penny, a small coin

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another

parts.note: rent is a regular payment for a home
a side is a team of players

explanation.surface: A head of state hands out small change to a team in their rent.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of a country, company or society is its chief.

clue.text: Study tear in new receptacle '

parts.note: to con is to study or learn

indicators.note: new means the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Examine a rip in a fresh box.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray ' in the clue is a print mark, not part of the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that holds other things is a vessel or box.

clue.text: Coming back to clear an abysmal situation

indicators.note: coming back means the letters of the pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: to clear something is to rid it

explanation.surface: Returning to tidy up a dreadful state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: The lowest possible point, the bottom of the abyss, is the nadir.
